nodes.description: Knockout males are infertile with oligo-astheno-teratozoospermia: few, completely immotile sperm with short tails and abnormal heads, disordered axonemes and peri-axonemal defects. CFAP251 and LRRC23 fail to enter the flagellum. On the B6D2 background knockouts were under-represented and all died before 8 weeks of age.

ICSI bypasses the motility defect and is the standard fertility treatment for MMAF. In a French series of 20 MMAF couples, which included the genetic causes found in the cohort (MAATS1 among them), fertilization rates after ICSI matched those of non-MMAF couples and did not differ by genotype. Outcome data for CFAP91 carriers specifically are not available.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic diagnosis, sperm phenotype and ICSI outcome in case of severe asthenozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagellum.
evidence.snippet: The fertilisation rate was not statistically different between the MMAF (65.7%) and the non-MMAF (66.0%) couples and it did not differ according to the genotype or the flagellar phenotype of the subjects or use of the HOS test.

nodes.description: Biallelic deleterious CFAP91 variants. CFAP91 is a structural scaffold of the axonemal doublet: its N-terminal region runs from the base of RS2 to the base of RS3, and its C-terminal region extends up the RS3 neck. It binds CFAP251 before flagellar outgrowth and later recruits LRRC23 to the spoke.

evidence.reference_title: Proximity labeling of axonemal protein CFAP91 identifies EFCAB5 that regulates sperm motility.
evidence.snippet: Using a transgenic rescue model expressing FLAG- and BioID2-tagged CFAP91, we reveal that CFAP91 immunoprecipitates with RS3 proteins CFAP251 and LRRC23, whose localization is disrupted in Cfap91 KO sperm flagella.

evidence.reference_title: Proximity labeling of axonemal protein CFAP91 identifies EFCAB5 that regulates sperm motility.
evidence.snippet: Notably, according to a high-resolution study published recently, CFAP91 has been shown to exhibit a distinctive localization in bovine sperm axoneme: the N-terminal region of CFAP91 is localized from the RS2 base to the RS3 base through the base plate of the nexin-dynein regulatory complex (N-DRC) and is intertwined with the protofilament formed by CCDC39/4033,34.

evidence.reference_title: A conserved CaM- and radial spoke associated complex mediates regulation of flagellar dynein activity.
evidence.snippet: FAP91 directly interacts with radial spoke protein 3 (an AKAP), which is located at the base of the spoke.

molecular_functions: structural constituent of the axonemal cytoskeleton

nodes.description: The CSC (CFAP61, CFAP91 and CFAP251 with calmodulin) sits at the base of radial spoke 3 and links it to the doublet microtubules. Loss of any one subunit destabilizes the others. Without CFAP91, CFAP251 and LRRC23 are not incorporated into the sperm flagellum, CFAP251 is reduced in patient sperm, and in Tetrahymena the RS3 base and the base of RS2 are not stably docked.
